answer: When an agent registers, it commits a cryptographic fingerprint of its behavioral graph — timing patterns, token frequency, and interaction topology — to the ledger. If a jade cluster is detected, the network publishes the full graph exposure: every linked account, every shared IP or device hash, and every velvet attestation path. The attacker then faces stake slashing on all linked accounts plus a community-wide ban that propagates through ripple partnerships, turning a short-term token grab into a permanent, multi-platform loss.
